column1: # The gate suite CI runs, with the arguments CI passes.
# COLUMN 1: the gate's name. A python gate is the script's file name; a
#           compiled gate is the subcommand of the binary.
# COLUMN 2: the command the harness runs, with the arguments the workflow
#           passes. The VALUE of an artifact path is the harness's business
#           (an empty directory of the right shape, see the README); the
#           FLAGS are the gate's business, and the gate that checks this
#           file compares them with the workflow's.
# The rows are the gates a workflow really runs. A gate CI runs only as its
# own self-test, a gate that needs the .NET SDK and a gate that needs the
# network are NOT here: they are in bench/gates/excluded.tsv, with the reason
# each of them is out. The set is checked by the gate
# `harbor-gates check-gate-bench-set`, which reads this file, the exclusion
# list and the workflow files, and fails when they disagree.
# The order is the order CI runs them in, roughly: the cheap text gates
# first, the gates that walk the git history last. The gates that read an
# artifact the build produced (the TRX files, the packed NuGet packages, the
# coverage report, the analyzer's log) are measured against an EMPTY
# directory of the right shape, so their number is the cost of walking the
# tree, not the cost of parsing a real artifact. The README says so, and the
# README says which artifact belongs to which row.
# The last row rewrites the mtimes of the tree, so it is last.

column2: python3 tools/aot-publish-gate.py --log publish/aot-publish.log --baseline .github/aot-warning-baseline.txt --expect-rid linux-x64 --expect-recipe fulltree --expect-status published

tools/bin/harbor-gates-linux-x64 coverage-report --coverage-dir Coverage --source-root . --registry tools/coverage-registry.txt --summary Coverage/summary.md --out Coverage/coverage-per-file.md --uncovered-out Coverage/coverage-uncovered-locations.txt --min-files 1200
